why: The answer says main() without String[] args is fine, which contradicts the Java rule: the class still compiles, but java Hello fails to launch because no main method is found.

concepts.quote: main() without String[] args is fine because the program uses no arguments.
concepts.why: Uses a wrong rule; the launcher needs the exact header public static void main(String[] args) whether or not args is used.

concepts.quote: because the program uses no arguments
concepts.why: Treats the args parameter as optional when unused, but it is part of the required entry-point signature.

concepts.quote: main() without String[] args is fine
concepts.why: Implies java Hello would run, but the launch fails with a no-main-method error.
